answer: Synchronized memory-hard puzzles deter Sybils by requiring every agent to populate a multi-gigabyte DRAM table from an unpredictable epoch seed and pass pointer-chasing lookups within a brief concurrent window. Because parallel deadlines block time-sharing one pool of RAM across clones, attackers must provision dedicated memory capacity and bus bandwidth per identity. Still, this excludes tiny battery nodes, like a mesh vertex tracking sparrow migrations along an ocean coast.
